title: Amazon rebuilds its advertising stack around an AI agent
subtitle: Amazon Ads Agent, unveiled at unBoxed 2026, merges the former DSP and Ads Console into a single conversational platform — natural-language targeting, agentic media planning, and automated performance analysis.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Amazon announced Amazon Ads Agent at unBoxed 2026 on September 29, folding its demand-side platform and former Ads Console into a single AI-first platform. The product unifies three campaign types — sponsored ads, Full-Funnel Campaigns, and the newly rebranded DVA (Display, Video, and Audio) — into one surface. Advertisers describe their desired audience in plain language, and the system returns targeting recommendations across products, categories, keywords, and Amazon audiences. The agent also handles media planning: audience sizing, reach forecasting, budget allocation, and incremental-reach comparison across channels, all conversationally. Full-Funnel Campaigns are in open beta for U.S. sellers now, with DVA rollout starting in late October.

The structural move matters more than the feature list. For a decade, enterprise advertising platforms have been self-service dashboards: filter panels, bidding knobs, dense reports. Amazon has now bet that the correct interface is a chat window and that the agent is the product. This matches moves at Google (AI-first ad buying in Search Ads 360), Meta (Advantage+ fully automated campaigns), and TikTok (Smart+ performance bidding) — but Amazon goes further by consolidating the DSP and the self-serve console into one agentic surface rather than keeping them as separate products with agent overlays.

The broader signal is about where agents land first in enterprise. Advertising operations is high-volume, high-feedback, and tolerant of imperfect decisions because every campaign is tested against measurable KPIs within hours. That is an ideal shape for an agent product: the agent cannot hide bad judgment because performance metrics expose it quickly, and the feedback loop lets the system improve. Expect the same pattern to show up next in retail-media buying for other platforms, then in SEO and content ops, then in customer-service routing — any workflow with a tight numerical feedback loop and a lot of repetitive decision-making.

A note for learners entering marketing, performance analytics, or related operations roles: the junior work that used to make up the first two years of these careers — pulling reports, running audience experiments, writing campaign briefs — is largely what Ads Agent now does by itself. The skills that still differentiate are judgement about which experiments to run, which creative strategies to test, and how to interpret ambiguous results. Lean into those from day one. The learning curve is steeper, but the comparative advantage is far more durable than report-building was.
